decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Add / edit / delete bookmarks (URL, title, description, tags)”. Round 1 client: “I can save… bookmarks.”
decisions.note: Implementation-review presentation records URL-based bookmark creation, conforming to the reference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Add / edit… bookmarks (URL, title, description, tags)”. Round 1 client: “I can… edit… bookmarks.”
decisions.note: The presented add and edit flows allow title and description to be supplied before saving and changed afterward; automatic collection is assessed separately under REF-BM-02.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker enumerates editable fields as “URL, title, description, tags”, omitting a note field and markdown-note rendering. Round 1 client gives only general approval: “I’m happy with the app as it is.”
decisions.note: At implementation review, the explicitly enumerated bookmark-editing schema lacks the required note field and markdown-note functionality. The client neither identifies nor corrects that difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Add / edit / delete bookmarks”. Round 1 client: “I can… remove bookmarks.”
decisions.note: Bookmark deletion is expressly presented and acknowledged, conforming to the reference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: bookmarks include “tags” and “Tags — comma-separated”. Round 1 client: “I can… organize… bookmarks.”
decisions.note: Comma-separated tag entry supports assigning one or more tags and is functionally conforming.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Tags — comma-separated, with clickable filter chips.” Round 1 client accepts the app as presented.
decisions.note: Clickable tag-filter chips provide the required specific-tag filtering behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Live search across title, URL, description, and tags”; the enumerated searchable fields omit note. Round 1 client says only “I can… find… bookmarks” and “I’m happy with the app as it is.”
decisions.note: The presented search scope diverges because REF-BM-12 also requires searching bookmark notes. General satisfaction does not explicitly surface or accept that difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker offers the absent capability as a future addition: “Want me to add anything — favicon/link previews…?” Round 1 client responds generally: “I’m happy with the app as it is.”
decisions.note: The future-feature offer establishes that required favicon/link-preview metadata collection is not in the presented implementation. The client does not mention the difference, so the approval is not an accepted divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker offers “import/export (e.g. browser HTML bookmarks)” as something that could be added. Round 1 client gives general approval without discussing import: “I’m happy with the app as it is.”
decisions.note: At implementation review, browser-HTML import is presented as absent. The client does not explicitly identify or accept that departure.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker offers “import/export (e.g. browser HTML bookmarks)” as something that could be added. Round 1 client gives general approval without discussing export: “I’m happy with the app as it is.”
decisions.note: At implementation review, browser-HTML export is presented as absent. The client does not explicitly identify or accept that departure.
